findings.anchor: .loop/plans/apm-only-install.md (Decided by the operator, How the install names the package)
findings.claim: The migration story covers only claude-plugin installs. A repository on the ADR 0013 route already has JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm#v0.3.0 as a string entry in its apm.yml, and an APM-owned kmctl SessionStart entry in .claude/settings.json (tagged by APM with _apm_source). The plan says install writes {git, path: apm, ref} into apm.yml but not that it replaces an existing kmctl entry in another form. If both entries stay, the old v0.3.0 package (git: parent, path: plugin) keeps deploying its skills and hook next to the new ones ('last installed wins'). If kmctl's hook writer takes over the old APM-owned entry in place and keeps its _apm_source, a later apm install removes it as stale.

Removing kmctl@kmctl may not stop things loading twice. The old marketplace entry declares okf@scaccogatto as a dependency (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json), so old installs also have the okf Claude plugin, and the old install added the scaccogatto and kmctl marketplaces at the chosen scope. The new route deploys okf's skills and Stop hook through APM. If claude plugin uninstall kmctl@kmctl --scope project leaves okf@scaccogatto installed, okf's skills and Stop hook run twice, which defeats the plan's stated aim ('so no skill loads twice'). The kmctl marketplace entry also stays behind, pointing at the staged folder that nothing refreshes any more.

ADR 0013-route consumers were not migrated. The plan now runs apm uninstall on the old entry before rewriting apm.yml, and spike:apm-only-install/6 shows that this removes the old hook and files and leaves one kmctl entry across two installs.
The okf plugin and marketplaces left by old installs. The plan now runs uninstall, prune and marketplace remove, backed by spike:apm-only-install/7.

Two okf MCP servers for repositories that followed today's APM how-to. docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md tells ADR 0013 users to get okf's MCP server by adding scaccogatto/okf-skills to their apm.yml. In that case okf is a direct dependency, so APM writes its server as `bundle` into .mcp.json (spike:kmctl-doctor/3, lock mcp_configs.bundle). The migration in Old installs (b) uninstalls only the JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm entry, so the direct okf-skills entry and its `bundle` server stay. kmctl then adds `okf-bundle` beside it: two okf servers that expose the same three tools. The plan should say what install does when apm.yml names okf-skills directly, or .mcp.json already holds an APM-managed okf server. For example, it could remove the direct entry with apm uninstall (kmctl's package pins okf anyway), or skip its own server and report this. r6b should then cover that case. The --trust-transitive-mcp variant is fine: APM's uninstall drops stale managed servers (apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py _cleanup_stale_mcp).
